recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Any future normative work to specify document signature generation should be handled as a new work-group issue, not as a FHIR-7033 reconciliation change.
issue_request: FHIR-7033 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 Composition issue asking for more documentation of the `$document` operation's `cert` parameter, explaining that it represented a keychain/private-key capability and recommending that signature generation be handled by the client or moved out of FHIR core. The accepted resolution was to remove the parameter and leave a note that signature generation was an open issue for DSTU 2.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 6194, preserved in git as 82c930a9240ac787a4ba7d7c36c4b1a2977280cf. That commit removed `document.cert` and `document.pword` rows from `source/composition/composition-spreadsheet.xml` and added a note that the operation did not resolve how document signatures are created.
additional_context: Composition is active in the current build through `source/fhir.ini`, and `source/composition/list-Composition-operations.xml` references `OperationDefinition/Composition-document`. Later refactors moved the operation to `source/composition/operationdefinition-Composition-document.xml` and preserved the signature note; `source/composition/composition-notes.xml` repeats the same trial-use note. Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant discussion that conflicts with the Jira/source evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current `$document` OperationDefinition lists only `persist`, `graph`, and `return` parameters, with no `cert`, `pword`, keychain, private-key, or passphrase input, and it still states that document signature generation remains unresolved.
